notes: §1985:VI.6.13.2 prints EVALUATE with selection subjects joined by ALSO (identifier, literal, expression, TRUE, FALSE), groups of WHEN phrases each closed by imperative-statement-1, an optional '[WHEN OTHER imperative-statement-2]' and END-EVALUATE; an object is ANY, a condition, TRUE, FALSE, or [NOT] an identifier, literal or arithmetic expression with an optional THROUGH operand. The grammar rules hold the shape at every edition and the 2002 additions are refused at --std 85 by COBOL0900: the partial-expression object (now gated in EvaluateBinder.BindWhenItem, kb/Work PB5179, closing the prior PARTIAL), boolean subjects/objects (VisitEvaluateSubject/VisitEvaluateWhenItem), the range's IN alphabet-name (RangeAlphabet) and address-identifier operands. Probed at 85: refused WHEN > 3, WHEN NOT < 3, WHEN NUMERIC, a bare class-name object, IN alphabet, NOT ANY (COBOL3710), only WHEN OTHER, WHEN OTHER twice, an empty WHEN group, a missing subject, objects without ALSO, a doubled THRU, a short object set (COBOL2106), boolean literals; accepted and correct: ZERO, group, signed range, ALL/SPACES/literal, TRUE ALSO FALSE, ODO element and ref-mod subjects, period-terminated form. The witness runs five EVALUATEs over the 1985 object forms. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB398 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5179 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-08.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-08-refute.json).
